To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high-Z contrast agents can be used to improve image quality in contrast-enhanced computed Tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis and that high-Z contrast media can be used for CT angiography of the lower extremities.

1) high-Z contrast agents can be used to enhance the CT attenuation of the human body; 2) the enhancement is sufficient to improve image quality in a wide range of applications, such as CT colonography and CT angiography; 3) the enhancement is also sufficient to improve the accuracy of CT-based attenuation correction in PET/CT; and 4) the enhancement is sufficiently large to allow the use of high-Z contrast for the detection of lung nodules.

high-Z contrast agents have the potential to be a useful adjunct to conventional contrast-enhanced CT in the future, and that the use of high-Z agents is limited by the availability of high-Z elements and by the need to use a large amount of contrast agent to achieve a clinically relevant enhancement.
